title: SC: Gratuity Can't Be Withheld For A Pending Appeal Against Acquittal
seo_title: SC: Gratuity Valid Despite Pending Appeal
case_name: Delhi Development Authority v. Rajender Kumar Sharma & Anr.
card_summary: The Supreme Court held that a retired employee's gratuity cannot be withheld merely because the State's appeal against an acquittal is still pending. The bench dismissed DDA's appeals and upheld a Delhi High Court ruling affirming a CAT direction to release gratuity withheld from two employees acquitted after a full trial, subject to an undertaking to refund it if the pending proceedings eventually go against them.
card_tip: An acquittal after trial is a final order for gratuity purposes; a department cannot keep withholding dues merely because it has filed, or may file, a further appeal, absent a stay.
verification_notes: AUDIENCE: domestic (government and PSU retirees). TARGET QUERY: can gratuity be withheld if the state appeals an acquittal. DEMAND EVIDENCE: none seen. Confirmed from LiveLaw and Verdictum reports of the 16 Nov 2026 judgment in Delhi Development Authority v. Rajender Kumar Sharma, 2026 INSC 1213 (Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar). Secondary reports differ slightly on the exact civil appeal numbers (14204-14205 or 14205 of 2026) and on one employee's original post; the core holding and outcome are consistent across all sources checked.
